Lecture 22

The principal series of SL⁡(2,R)\SL(2,\R)SL(2,R)

What this lecture does

This lecture builds the principal series of G=SL⁡(2,R)G=\SL(2,\R)G=SL(2,R). The principal series is induced from characters of the upper triangular subgroup. We realise it on functions on a circle. We prove unitarity when the parameter is purely imaginary. Then we compute how the Lie algebra moves vectors between KKK-types. Finally we use this ladder to decide which of these representations are irreducible.

22.5 Closed invariant subspaces

We now pass from the module Vε,νV_{\varepsilon,\nu}Vε,ν​ to the Hilbert representation on Hε\mathcal H_\varepsilonHε​. A (g,K)(\g,K)(g,K)-submodule is an algebraic object and a closed invariant subspace is an analytic one, so the submodule criterion does not settle the question alone. In general the passage between them is Harish-Chandra’s correspondence for admissible representations. For this family we prove what we need directly. First, a closed invariant subspace contains Fourier vectors. Next, a half-ladder has an invariant closed span.

The representation Πε,ν\Pi_{\varepsilon,\nu}Πε,ν​ on Hε\mathcal H_\varepsilonHε​ has no closed invariant subspace other than 000 and Hε\mathcal H_\varepsilonHε​ exactly when ν∉ε+1+2Z\nu\notin\varepsilon+1+2\mathbb{Z}ν∈/ε+1+2Z. Reducibility. Let ν∈ε+1+2Z\nu\in\varepsilon+1+2\mathbb{Z}ν∈ε+1+2Z. Then ν=n−1\nu=n-1ν=n−1 or ν=−(n−1)\nu=-(n-1)ν=−(n−1) for an integer n≥1n\ge1n≥1 with n≡ε(mod2)n\equiv\varepsilon\pmod 2n≡ε(mod2). By Proposition 22.18, Hn+H_n^+Hn+​ or its orthogonal complement is a closed invariant subspace in the two cases. Each is nonzero and proper.

The imaginary axis. A number ν∈iR\nu\in i\Rν∈iR lies in ε+1+2Z\varepsilon+1+2\mathbb{Z}ε+1+2Z only for ν=0\nu=0ν=0 and ε=1\varepsilon=1ε=1. So the exception is Π1,0\Pi_{1,0}Π1,0​.

The point (1,0)(1,0)(1,0). Take n=1n=1n=1. Then H1+H_1^+H1+​ and H1−H_1^-H1−​ are invariant, mutually orthogonal, and together they span H1\mathcal H_1H1​. For odd n≥1n\ge1n≥1 we have 1+n≠01+n\neq01+n=0, and for odd n≥3n\ge3n≥3 we have 1−n≠01-n\neq01−n=0. So the ladder puts every ene_nen​ with odd n≥1n\ge1n≥1 in WWW. Hence W=H1+W=H_1^+W=H1+​. The pieces at the reducibility points return in Lecture 23.

The reducible module at (ε,ν)=(1,0)(\varepsilon,\nu)=(1,0)(ε,ν)=(1,0)

The simplest reducibility point is (ε,ν)=(1,0)(\varepsilon,\nu)=(1,0)(ε,ν)=(1,0). The Fourier labels are the odd integers, and the ladder formulas become dΠ(X+)en=(1+n)en+2,dΠ(X−)en=(1−n)en−2.d\Pi(X_+)e_n=(1+n)e_{n+2},\qquad d\Pi(X_-)e_n=(1-n)e_{n-2}.dΠ(X+​)en​=(1+n)en+2​,dΠ(X−​)en​=(1−n)en−2​. At n=−1n=-1n=−1, the upward coefficient vanishes. At n=1n=1n=1, the downward coefficient vanishes. Thus the space V1,0V_{1,0}V1,0​ is the direct sum V1,0=span⁡{e1,e3,e5,…} ⊕ span⁡{e−1,e−3,e−5,…}.V_{1,0}=\Span\{e_1,e_3,e_5,\ldots\} \ \oplus\ \Span\{e_{-1},e_{-3},e_{-5},\ldots\}.V1,0​=span{e1​,e3​,e5​,…} ⊕ span{e−1​,e−3​,e−5​,…}. Each summand is preserved by both ladder operators and by KKK. Within either chain, the remaining connecting coefficients are nonzero. The weight-projection argument in the proof of the submodule criterion (Proposition 22.15) shows that each chain is algebraically irreducible.

The irreducibility theorem (Theorem 22.19) gives the two closed irreducible summands. Their group invariance is Proposition 22.18, which goes beyond the algebraic calculation above. Lecture 23 identifies them as limits of discrete series and explains their norms. The full odd ladder breaks at the gap between −1-1−1 and 111.

For comparison, (ε,ν)=(0,0)(\varepsilon,\nu)=(0,0)(ε,ν)=(0,0) has only even labels. Neither equation 1+n=01+n=01+n=0 nor 1−n=01-n=01−n=0 has an even solution. Its algebraic module is therefore irreducible.

22.7 Summary

The principal series Πε,ν\Pi_{\varepsilon,\nu}Πε,ν​ is induced from the character σε⊗eνt\sigma_\varepsilon\otimes e^{\nu t}σε​⊗eνt of P=MANP=MANP=MAN, shifted by ΔP1/2\Delta_P^{1/2}ΔP1/2​. Restriction to KKK identifies every Iε,νI_{\varepsilon,\nu}Iε,ν​ with the continuous parity-ε\varepsilonε functions on the circle. The group acts on these functions by the circle-model formula (22.4). The identity τh′=∣huθ∣−2\tau_h'=|hu_\theta|^{-2}τh′​=∣huθ​∣−2 makes the pairing of ν\nuν with −νˉ-\bar\nu−νˉ invariant. Hence, for ν∈iR\nu\in i\Rν∈iR, the operators Πε,ν(g)\Pi_{\varepsilon,\nu}(g)Πε,ν​(g) extend to a strongly continuous unitary representation on Hε\mathcal H_\varepsilonHε​.

Each KKK-type occurring in Vε,νV_{\varepsilon,\nu}Vε,ν​ occurs once and is spanned by one ene_nen​ with n≡ε(mod2)n\equiv\varepsilon\pmod2n≡ε(mod2). The elements X±X_\pmX±​ move nnn by ±2\pm2±2 with coefficients ν+1±n\nu+1\pm nν+1±n. We proved that the (g,K)(\g,K)(g,K)-module Vε,νV_{\varepsilon,\nu}Vε,ν​ is reducible exactly at integers ν\nuν of parity opposite to ε\varepsilonε. We also proved the same criterion for closed invariant subspaces of Hε\mathcal H_\varepsilonHε​. Fourier projection and the ladder give irreducibility away from these points. At ν=n−1\nu=n-1ν=n−1 the power series of (22.6) show that the closed span of the half-ladder k≥nk\ge nk≥n is invariant, and at ν=−(n−1)\nu=-(n-1)ν=−(n−1) its orthogonal complement is. At (ε,ν)=(1,0)(\varepsilon,\nu)=(1,0)(ε,ν)=(1,0) the two half-ladders split H1\mathcal H_1H1​ into irreducible summands. The module equivalence of ±ν\pm\nu±ν and its unitary version stay cited.
